title: Tool Use & Function Calling
subtitle: Defining tools and parsing structured outputs
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: LLMs are text-in, text-out. They can't retrieve live data, run code, or interact with external systems on their own. Pure text responses can't reliably produce machine-parseable structured output.
whyItExists.solution: Tool use (function calling) gives LLMs a structured way to request actions from your code. The model returns a typed JSON tool call; your code executes it and returns the result. This bridges LLMs to real-world systems.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Whenever the LLM needs data it doesn't have (weather, database queries, API calls), needs to perform actions (send email, write file), or when you need guaranteed structured JSON output.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Simple Q&A that the model can answer from training data. Adding tools increases latency and cost — only add tools the model will actually use.

explainModes.beginner: Think of tools as buttons the AI can press. You tell it 'you can press the weather button (give it a city name)' and 'you can press the database button (give it a SQL query)'. The AI decides when to press them and your code does the actual work.
explainModes.simple: You define a list of functions your code can run (search database, send email, etc.) and describe them to the LLM. When the model needs data it doesn't have, it returns a structured tool call instead of text. Your code runs the function, returns the result, and the model continues.
explainModes.standard: Tool use is a two-turn pattern: (1) Send messages + tool definitions → model returns tool_use content blocks; (2) Execute the tools in your code, add tool_result blocks, re-send → model generates final text answer. The model decides whether to use tools based on the tool descriptions.
explainModes.technical: Anthropic's tool use uses JSON Schema for input validation. The model returns content blocks with type='tool_use', name, id, and input (typed JSON). Your code maps names to functions, executes them, then sends back tool_result blocks with the tool_use_id. The model then reasons over results and returns stop_reason='end_turn'.
explainModes.deepDive: Tools enable structured output extraction by defining an output schema as a 'fake' tool. Set tool_choice={'type':'tool','name':'extract'} to force the model to always call a specific tool — this is the most reliable way to get guaranteed JSON output. Parallel tool calls (multiple tool_use blocks in one response) allow the model to batch independent calls.

content.text: Tools (function calling) let the LLM request data or actions from your code. The model returns a structured tool call; you execute it and return the result. This gives LLMs access to real-time data, databases, APIs, and any capability your code can provide.

content.definition: A JSON Schema description of a function: its name, description (what it does, when to use it), and input_schema (the typed parameters). The model decides whether and when to call tools based entirely on these descriptions.
The output your code returns after executing a tool call. Sent back as a tool_result message with the matching tool_use_id. The model reads the result and decides what to do next.

content.code:
import anthropic, json
client = anthropic.Anthropic()

def get_weather(city: str, units: str = "celsius") -> dict:
    """Your actual implementation — calls a real weather API."""
    # Stub for demo
    return {"city": city, "temperature": 18, "units": units, "condition": "Partly cloudy"}

tools = [{"name": "get_weather", "description": "Get current weather",
          "input_schema": {"type": "object",
                           "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}, "units": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius","fahrenheit"]}},
                           "required": ["city"]}}]

messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Tokyo and in London?"}]

# Agentic loop
while True:
    response = client.messages.create(
        model="claude-haiku-5-5", max_tokens=1024, tools=tools, messages=messages
    )

    if response.stop_reason == "end_turn":
        print(response.content[0].text)
        break

    # Collect all tool calls (may be multiple)
    tool_results = []
    for block in response.content:
        if block.type == "tool_use":
            result = get_weather(**block.input)
            tool_results.append({
                "type": "tool_result",
                "tool_use_id": block.id,
                "content": json.dumps(result)
            })

    # Add assistant response + tool results, continue
    messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response.content})
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": tool_results})

content.text: The most reliable way to get guaranteed JSON output is to define an extraction tool and force the model to always call it using tool_choice. This avoids the model outputting markdown, explanations, or malformed JSON.

content.code:
import anthropic, json
client = anthropic.Anthropic()

# Define an extraction schema as a 'fake' tool
extract_tool = {
    "name": "extract_contact",
    "description": "Extract contact information from text",
    "input_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
            "name": {"type": "string"},
            "email": {"type": "string"},
            "company": {"type": "string"},
            "phone": {"type": ["string", "null"]}
        },
        "required": ["name", "email", "company"]
    }
}

text = "Reach out to Aisha Patel at aisha@technova.io — she heads engineering at TechNova."

response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-haiku-5-5",
    max_tokens=512,
    tools=[extract_tool],
    tool_choice={"type": "tool", "name": "extract_contact"},  # force this tool
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": f"Extract contact info from: {text}"}]
)

tool_block = next(b for b in response.content if b.type == "tool_use")
contact = tool_block.input  # Guaranteed well-typed dict
print(json.dumps(contact, indent=2))

content.text: Write clear, specific tool descriptions. The model decides whether and when to call tools based entirely on them. 'Get weather for a city' is better than 'weather tool'.
Never give the LLM tools with dangerous side effects (delete database, send real emails) unless you have a human-in-the-loop confirmation step. Always validate tool inputs before executing them.

questions.question: Who executes the tool when an LLM requests a function call?
options: The LLM itself — it has built-in execution
Your application code — the LLM only returns a structured call request
The API server sandboxes and runs it
A separate subprocess spawned by the SDK
questions.explanation: The LLM returns a tool_use block with name and input. Your code maps the name to a real function, runs it, and sends the result back. The LLM never executes code.

questions.question: What is the most reliable way to get guaranteed JSON output from an LLM?
options: Define an extraction tool and use tool_choice to force the model to always call it
Instruct the model in the system prompt to only output JSON
questions.explanation: Forced tool use (tool_choice) guarantees the model outputs a structured JSON tool call that matches your schema. This is more reliable than prompting for JSON, which the model may format inconsistently.

questions.question: What does stop_reason='tool_use' mean in an Anthropic response?
options: The model stopped because it used a tool and is done
The model wants your code to execute one or more tools and return the results
The model ran out of tools to use
An error occurred in tool execution
questions.explanation: stop_reason='tool_use' means the model generated tool_use content blocks and is waiting for your code to execute the tools and send back tool_result messages so it can continue.

faq.q: Can I give a model multiple tools?
faq.a: Yes. Pass an array of tool definitions. The model selects the most appropriate one(s), or none if it can answer without a tool. It may also call multiple tools in parallel (one per content block).

faq.q: What is the difference between tool_choice 'auto' and 'tool'?
faq.a: 'auto' (default) lets the model decide whether to use tools. {'type': 'tool', 'name': 'X'} forces a specific tool — use this for guaranteed structured output extraction.
Not directly — the model calls tools, your code executes them. But in an agentic loop, the model can call tool A, see the result, then call tool B based on that result — effectively chaining tools.

usedIn: AI assistants that query live databases or APIs
LLM-powered automation that sends emails or creates calendar events
Code generation assistants that execute test runners
examples: A travel assistant that calls flight search and hotel booking APIs based on user intent
A data extraction service that forces JSON output via tool_choice for downstream database ingestion
